note: The Sultanate of Rum occupied territory that Byzantium considered its heartland; the two states competed for Anatolia for two centuries. Byzantine attempts to reconquer the Anatolian plateau failed at Myriokephalon (1176). The Fourth Crusade's sack of Constantinople (1204) temporarily reduced Byzantine pressure on Rum.

_quarry.structural_significance: The Sultanate of Rum's progressive occupation of Byzantine Anatolia converted the demographic base of the Byzantine army and tax system from Greek to Turkish over two centuries; the irreversibility of this Turkification—reinforced by continuous nomadic migration—meant that even Byzantine reconquest of territories would have found a transformed population, making permanent Byzantine recovery of Anatolia structurally impossible after c. 1200.
